gaps.concept: Precocious puberty begins before age 8 in girls or 9 in boys; delayed puberty means no breasts by 13 or testicular enlargement by 14.
gaps.why_tested: Age and physical findings determine whether a vignette describes abnormal pubertal timing.

gaps.concept: In boys, testicular volume of at least 4 mL marks gonadarche; pubic hair alone does not establish true puberty.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes early testicular maturation from isolated adrenarche.

gaps.concept: LH stimulates Leydig-cell testosterone production; FSH supports Sertoli cells and spermatogenesis and stimulates ovarian granulosa-cell aromatase.
gaps.why_tested: Links gonadotropin changes to the source of pubertal sex steroids.

gaps.concept: Sex steroids increase growth through GH–IGF-1; estrogen drives epiphyseal maturation and closure in both sexes.
gaps.why_tested: Explains why early puberty initially accelerates growth but can reduce adult height.

gaps.concept: Central precocious puberty follows the usual sequence with bilateral testicular enlargement; peripheral androgen excess may cause virilization without testicular enlargement.
gaps.why_tested: An early-virilizing boy’s testicular size distinguishes central from peripheral puberty.

gaps.concept: Hypothalamic hamartoma can cause central precocious puberty with gelastic seizures.
gaps.why_tested: Episodes of inappropriate laughter accompany early pubertal development.

gaps.concept: Familial male-limited precocious puberty (testotoxicosis) results from activating LHCGR mutations, producing testosterone despite suppressed gonadotropins.
gaps.why_tested: A boy has familial early virilization and high testosterone with low LH.

gaps.concept: hCG-secreting tumors stimulate Leydig-cell LH receptors, causing testosterone-mediated precocity in boys despite suppressed pituitary LH.
gaps.why_tested: A boy has elevated hCG, high testosterone, and low LH.

gaps.concept: Granulosa-cell tumors secrete estrogen and can cause early breast development or bleeding; Leydig-cell tumors secrete androgens and cause virilization.
gaps.why_tested: The sex steroid pattern identifies the tumor behind peripheral precocity.

gaps.concept: In 21-hydroxylase deficiency, elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone and adrenal androgens cause early pubarche with suppressed gonadotropins.
gaps.why_tested: A child has early androgenic signs without gonadal maturation.

gaps.concept: McCune–Albright syndrome arises from a postzygotic mosaic GNAS mutation; autonomous ovarian estrogen production can cause episodic vaginal bleeding.
gaps.why_tested: Recurrent bleeding and asymmetric skin lesions accompany gonadotropin-independent puberty.

gaps.concept: Severe primary hypothyroidism can cause precocious breast development or bleeding with delayed bone age (Van Wyk–Grumbach syndrome).
gaps.why_tested: Delayed skeletal maturation distinguishes this presentation from typical precocious puberty.

gaps.concept: Premature thelarche has isolated breast development without accelerated growth or advanced bone age.
gaps.why_tested: An otherwise well young girl has breast budding without progressive puberty.

gaps.concept: Premature adrenarche causes pubic or axillary hair, body odor, and acne without breast development or testicular enlargement.
gaps.why_tested: Early hair growth occurs while the gonadal axis remains prepubertal.

gaps.concept: Pubertal gynecomastia reflects a transient increase in the estrogen-to-androgen effect during otherwise normal male puberty.
gaps.why_tested: A pubertal boy develops bilateral breast tissue without other evidence of disease.

gaps.concept: Hypogonadotropic delayed puberty has low sex steroids with low or inappropriately normal LH/FSH; primary gonadal failure has low sex steroids with high LH/FSH.
gaps.why_tested: Hormone results localize delayed puberty to the central axis or gonads.

gaps.concept: Kallmann syndrome results from failed migration of GnRH neurons from the olfactory placode; anosmia accompanies low LH/FSH and delayed puberty.
gaps.why_tested: An adolescent with absent puberty also reports impaired smell.

gaps.concept: Micropenis or cryptorchidism favors congenital GnRH deficiency over constitutional delay in a boy with late puberty.
gaps.why_tested: Early-life reproductive findings distinguish persistent hypogonadism from a late normal variant.

gaps.concept: Turner syndrome (45,X) causes streak ovaries, low estrogen, high FSH/LH, absent breast development, and primary amenorrhea; pubic hair may develop normally.
gaps.why_tested: A short adolescent has absent gonadarche despite preserved adrenal hair growth.

gaps.concept: Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY) causes small firm testes, seminiferous-tubule hyalinization, low testosterone, high FSH/LH, and often gynecomastia.
gaps.why_tested: A tall adolescent has incomplete virilization and persistently small testes.

gaps.concept: Chronic illness and hyperprolactinemia can suppress GnRH, producing functional hypogonadotropic delayed puberty.
gaps.why_tested: Systemic disease or elevated prolactin accompanies delayed maturation with low gonadotropins.
